2) Explain how Redwood treats caching: if a prompt is cached, do we avoid billing entirely for the request or is there still billed compute for lookup/metadata?

Subject: Re: Pricing metric clarification - tokens vs characters vs requests

Thanks Alex - good details. Quick answers and a worked example below. I\u2019ll also loop Rishi on reserved/dedicated options if volumes look like they\u2019ll be sustained.

1) Characters -> tokens conversion (rule of thumb):
   - For English, 1 token \u2248 4 characters on average (so 1M tokens \u2248 4M characters). This varies by language and punctuation; code or highly-tokenized text will change the ratio.

2) Example conversion & unit economics (your 350M characters/day):
   - Tokens/day \u2248 350,000,000 chars / 4 \u2248 87,500,000 tokens/day
   - Tokens/month (30-day) \u2248 2,625,000,000 tokens/month (~2.625B)

Cost at example price points (per 1M tokens):
   - $8 / 1M tokens -> (2,625 * $8) \u2248 $21,000 / month
   - $12 / 1M tokens -> (2,625 * $12) \u2248 $31,500 / month
   - $20 / 1M tokens -> (2,625 * $20) \u2248 $52,500 / month

Notes on billing vs requests vs caching:
- Billed units: Redwood bills based on tokens (prompt tokens + completion tokens) processed by the model for a given request.
- Requests metric (API calls) is useful for rate-limiting and concurrency planning but is not the billing unit. Even many small requests with small token counts can add up.
- Prompt caching: if a request is fully satisfied by a cache hit (we return a cached response without invoking the model), that request is not billed as model tokens. If we perform a model call (even for a short completion) the prompt+completion tokens are billed.
- Partial caching: we also support prefix/KV caching where cached key-value states reduce compute and latency for repeated prefixes - those optimizations reduce GPU cost but billing still counts tokens generated by the model call. The key exception is full cache hits (no model call).

Given your note that ~20-30 prompts are highly templated, we can model two scenarios:
A) Conservative: only those 30 prompts are cached -> estimated cache hit rate ~5-8% -> small billing reduction.
B) Optimistic: with additional business logic to canonicalize clinician prompts (normalization + template matching) you could increase effective caching to 20-25% for some flows.

3) Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm if the 350M char/day is peak or sustained daily average? If that\u2019s peak, please share average/day so we can model both.
- I\u2019ll run a short cost model for the three price points above and include two caching scenarios (30-template cache vs 25% effective cache).
- If monthly tokens remain > ~1B, Rishi can propose reserved capacity pricing (significant per-unit discounts) - Rishi, can you add a note with an example reserved tier?

I\u2019ll attach the worked example as a short spreadsheet in the follow-up. Happy to do a 20-minute call to walk procurement through the numbers.

- Marissa

Hi Alex - Rishi here from the pricing team. Quick note on reserved/dedicated options:

- At sustained volumes ~2.5B tokens/month, customers commonly move to a reserved capacity plan where effective unit price can drop substantially (example: $8- $10 / 1M tokens effective vs pay-as-you-go $12- $20). The exact numbers depend on commitment length and burst profile.
- Advantages: predictable monthly cost, capacity isolation (helpful for low-latency SLOs), and priority scaling.

If you\u2019re open, let\u2019s schedule a 20-30 minute pricing + procurement call next week to walk through options and I\u2019ll bring a sample commitment calc and contract timeline. How does Wednesday 10-10:30am PT look?

- Rishi
